tasks.short: Interview patients and measure vital signs

steps.what: Interview patients to obtain medical information and clarify their responses
Measure vital signs, weight and height and check measurement reliability
outputs: observed vital signs weight and height

tasks.design: Retain the patient interview and physical measurements, using existing measurement equipment {OTHER}. This task produces observations for the separate records task; no ambient scribe or pre-visit questionnaire is introduced here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant information must be elicited and measurements must be taken with the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment supports measurement; the digest's scribe evidence concerns documentation rather than this physical intake.
tasks.still_hard: Clarify sensitive information and notice unreliable readings or concerns requiring a clinician.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and respond to the patient's condition.
tasks.altitude: Reliable observations rather than less patient contact.

evidence.claim: A Dutch GP scribe study reduced documentation time but found no change in total consultation time.
That study does not establish savings in assistant interviews or physical measurements.

assumptions: Patient identification is an existing prerequisite; resolving identity uncertainty remains within the retained encounter time.
The assistant produces clarified information in s1 and actual readings in s2, with all acquisition and clarification time counted.
Recording those observations in the medical record is a separate task and is not added as a hidden saving here.
No new device connection or upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Current intake process and measurement equipment
research_questions: What proportion of intake time concerns clarification or repeat measurement?

already_counted.description: Interview and measurement time remain fully retained.

incremental.description: No changed workflow or new upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and no incremental work give zero saving. Documentation case results are not applied to physical intake.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record medical history, vital statistics and test results

steps.what: Identify the patient encounter and inspect source history, vital statistics and test results
outputs: identified source set and unresolved source questions

steps.what: Enter medical history, vital statistics and test results into the encounter record
inputs: identified source set and unresolved source questions

steps.what: Verify medical record entries against sources, correct discrepancies and release the checked version
inputs: identified source set and unresolved source questions

tasks.design: Configure approved source import into the existing clinical record {OTHER}, carrying patient, encounter, units, timestamps and provenance into draft entries. The assistant resolves source ambiguity, compares each entry to its source and releases only the checked version; narrative history stays manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Structured results and measurements are sometimes retyped between approved systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Native clinical record interfaces can reuse structured values without generating medical meaning; local interface support must be verified.
tasks.still_hard: Identify the correct encounter, distinguish corrected results and reconcile conflicting sources.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a semantically implausible entry and obtain clarification rather than silently normalising it.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time retyping and retain accountable source verification.

reach.task: Clarify result identity and correction status

evidence.claim: The digest proposes clinical record integration and order-derived labels as a deterministic approach, not a measured assistant outcome.

assumptions: The interviewing assistant produces source history and measurement records during acquisition; laboratory staff produce authorised results in the laboratory system. Their unchanged source capture is outside this recording-only task and earns no saving here.
Import requires source patient and encounter identifiers, test or observation code, value, unit, collection time, author and correction status; absent fields use full manual entry.
s1 includes locating and resolving source identity; s2 retains all narrative entry and import review; s3 retains verification and correction.
Use existing clinical record configuration before custom integration; no public chatbot or clinical inference.
This task's baseline excludes the separate patient interview and measurement task, preventing double credit.
unknowns: Native source interfaces and structured share
Whether source capture is already part of another recording baseline
research_questions: Does import reduce net entry time while preserving correct encounter, unit, timestamp and correction status?

already_counted.description: Source identification and final source comparison remain fully counted.
Manual narrative entry and import review remain counted.

incremental.description: Assistant reports interface discrepancies and reviews changed mappings.
Clinical systems administrator maintains source mappings and interface tests.

approvals.approved_version: Exact corrected draft encounter entries, their patient, encounter, values, units, timestamps and provenance; any source or entry change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 estimate B=100, R=25+18+30=73; gross 27 less 2 focal upkeep gives net 25. High requires supported structured sources and genuine retyping; low covers manual fallback or no removable re-entry. Acquisition time is excluded from both baseline and saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the physician's instructions and clarify the intended patient explanation
Explain treatment procedures, medications, diets or physician instructions and check patient understanding

tasks.design: Keep explanation with the assistant using the physician's instructions and approved information in the clinical record {OTHER}. No generated treatment advice or automatic patient messaging is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant must relate an authorised instruction to what this patient understands.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instructions and approved information support the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Respond to uncertainty, language barriers and questions beyond the assistant's scope.
tasks.human_edge: Detect misunderstanding and bring unanswered clinical questions to the physician.

evidence.claim: A documentation scribe does not establish that patient explanation and understanding checks can lose time.

assumptions: The physician produces the instructions in the existing care process; the assistant's reading and clarification remain in s1.
Approved information is already maintained by clinical staff; no new content feed or structured instruction code is required.
All explanation, questions and understanding checks remain in s2.
No new content generation or associated maintenance is introduced.
unknowns: Availability of approved information in patients' languages
research_questions: Which instructions repeatedly require physician clarification?

already_counted.description: Instruction clarification and patient explanation remain in full.

incremental.description: No new content system or upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; no incremental work and no new saving. Existing handouts do not remove patient conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect, log and prepare laboratory specimens

steps.what: Verify patient identity and laboratory orders and prepare collection supplies
Collect blood, tissue or other laboratory specimens and confirm specimen identity
Label and log specimens, prepare them for testing and confirm the laboratory handoff
outputs: labelled logged specimens prepared for testing

tasks.design: Retain collection, logging and preparation using the existing laboratory order and label tools {OTHER}. Order-derived labels are useful where already available, but their current benefit is in the baseline and no new specimen automation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collection and reliable specimen identity require physical work and careful handoff.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order and label tools support this workflow without a new model.
tasks.still_hard: Collect suitable material and maintain identity through preparation and transfer.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise collection difficulties and specimen problems requiring escalation.

reach.task: Clarify unsuitable specimens and handoff gaps
reach.learn: Which collection records support reliable testing

evidence.claim: Order-derived specimen labels are a deterministic workflow possibility, not a demonstrated new saving in this unchanged design.

assumptions: The ordering clinician produces the authorised order; existing order capture is outside this collection task.
The assistant verifies patient identity in s1, produces specimen identity, time and collector information in s2, and captures the log and handoff in s3; all time remains.
No free specimen status, automatic labelling or new interface is introduced.
No changed system means no incremental upkeep; this task's specimen log is distinct from recording final test results.
unknowns: Existing label and specimen tracking tools
research_questions: Where do specimen identity or handoff discrepancies arise in the current process?

already_counted.description: Verification, collection, logging and preparation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new label interface or upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 with zero incremental work yield no new saving. Existing label functionality is already in the baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain patient interaction and physical care while reducing supported record re-entry.
reach: Clarify source provenance with laboratory staff
Refer unresolved patient questions to clinicians
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with reliable source-linked records and preserved time for patient understanding and physical care.
